key_insight: Ti₇₆Nb₂₂Al₂ can support complex martensitic microstructures with an unchanged grain boundary and identity macroscopic deformation gradient, despite mutually incompatible local deformation states.
engineering_relevance: The analysis links transformation-strain compatibility to interface formation and grain-shape preservation, informing the design of shape-memory alloy microstructures.
method: Analyze 12 martensitic deformation matrices rank-one connected to austenite using the moving mask approximation.
Establish a degenerate T₁₂ configuration for unit middle eigenvalue and volume-preserving transformation, with microstructures supported on just 8 matrices.
Compare pairwise near-compatibility with experimentally observed interface frequencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental confirmation of the identity macroscopic deformation gradient and more frequent observation of interfaces between more nearly compatible matrix pairs.
watch_item: The existence result assumes exact unit middle eigenvalue and volume preservation and does not yield a deformation whose gradient lies in the finite matrix set almost everywhere.
paper_title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
